questions.stem: In a row file format, what happens when a user requests data from a single column?
options: Only that column is read into memory
The column is read from an index without touching the rows
The whole row is extracted into memory and the requested column is displayed
The request is rejected because row formats cannot serve single columns
The file is converted to columnar format first
questions.explanation: Row formats load the entire row into memory even when only one column is needed, then display that column.

questions.stem: In a columnar file format, what is extracted into memory when a user requests one column?
options: The first row of every column
questions.explanation: Columnar formats read only the requested column into memory, which is why they suit extraction for analysis.

questions.stem: A file has 100 columns and 1 million rows, and a user queries only 5 columns. What does a row file format load into memory?
options: 5 columns with a sample of rows
questions.explanation: The row format extracts all 100 columns for all 1 million rows, fully using memory although only 5 columns were needed.

questions.stem: Which file format type is best for ETL/ELT processing?
questions.explanation: Row file formats are best for ETL/ELT processing, whereas columnar formats suit data extraction for analysis.

questions.stem: Which file format type is best for extracting data for analysis?
questions.explanation: Columnar file formats load only the columns requested, making them best for data extraction for analysis.

questions.stem: Which of the commonly used big data file formats are human-readable, in ASCII or Unicode text?
questions.explanation: CSV and JSON are human-readable text formats; ORC, Avro and Parquet are binary and not human-readable.

questions.stem: Which file format is described as very CPU-intensive?
questions.explanation: Under performance considerations, JSON is singled out as a very CPU-intensive file format.

questions.stem: If a dataset requires nested data, which file formats are recommended?
questions.explanation: For nested data the choices are JSON, Avro and Parquet, with Avro suited to ETL/ELT and Parquet to querying.

questions.stem: Which formats are said to provide some degree of schema evolution?
questions.explanation: ORC, Avro and Parquet provide some degree of schema evolution.

questions.stem: What are the two normal kinds of data usage that should guide the choice of a big data file format?
questions.explanation: Data is normally used either to do ETL/ELT or to extract data, and the right file format depends on which is intended.
